evidence_quotes.quote: Estudio transversal con enfoque cualitativo, que muestra el análisis de la regulación que promueve el valor económico del agua en la legislación de las aguas nacionales, y la asequibilidad para la efectividad de los derechos de acceso, a través de las tarifas aproximadas que cubren los usuarios por los servicios públicos.
Se aplicaron dos encuestas con dos muestreos aleatorios estratificados (Mukherjee et al., 2022) a una población finita de 88,686 usuarios del SEAPAL-VALLARTA (SEAPAL, 2023).

Los artículos 4, 9, 14, 16, 18, 46, 51 y 58 del RPSPAPDATDARMPV establecen contribuciones y pagos de derechos que deberá realizar la población para solicitar la contratación de los servicios, cubrir las cuotas por la conexión a las redes e instalación de tomas y dictamen de factibilidad, así como la adhesión al contrato con el organismo operador para la prestación de los servicios.

La asequibilidad de las tarifas se promueve a su vez con las disposiciones del capítulo VII del RPSPAPDATDARMPV, que establecen subsidios para instituciones de asistencia social y uso doméstico, sin que estos rebasen el 50% de los costos del consumo y previo el cumplimiento de requisitos correspondientes, como se señala en la tabla 4.
Aun cuando el 60% de los usuarios D.C.I. manifiestan que el costo es accesible, se tiene al 38% que afirman costos elevados con 137 usuarios en este último porcentaje

el 66.20% de los usuarios D.C.I. se sienten seguros de contar con agua al hacer el pago por el suministro y 33.80% de estos usuarios afirman que dicho pago no les asegura el poder disponer del recurso hídrico.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines household/domestic (as well as commercial, industrial, and hotel) access to municipal drinking water and wastewater sanitation services provided by SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, it analyzes national, state, and municipal water legislation and regulatory governance. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, it examines concrete rule-type mechanisms directly governing service access and affordability: mandatory connection fees and contracting/feasibility requirements (RPSPAPDATDARMPV Arts. 4, 9, 14, 16, 18, 57, 58; Municipal Revenue Law Art. 56), volumetric tariff tiers (minimum quota, increasing block cost, and total cost under RPSPAPDATDARMPV Arts. 44, 46, 52), and domestic tariff subsidy eligibility screening rules requiring Mexican citizenship, owner/tenant residence, income qualification, no payment arrears, and consumption <= 60 m3 bimonthly capped at a 50% discount (RPSPAPDATDARMPV Chapter VII, Table 4).
criterion_notes.c3: Combines statutory/regulatory tariff analysis with primary empirical survey data from two stratified random samples of SEAPAL-VALLARTA utility users (n = 364 domestic/commercial/industrial users selected via QGIS across neighborhoods and n = 100 hotel users from a utility list, drawn from N = 88,686 total users), analyzed with descriptive statistics in SPSS 2021.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports empirical outcomes directly relevant to affordability and reliability/availability of municipal water and sanitation service: self-reported tariff payment ranges and volumetric tariff block placement (89.83% of D.C.I. users in increasing-cost blocks), perceived tariff affordability (60% accessible vs. 38% elevated among D.C.I. users), and perceived security of continuous water supply upon bill payment (66.20% secure vs. 33.80% insecure among D.C.I. users; 91% vs. 9% among hotel users).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (SEAPAL-VALLARTA utility user accounts/respondents in Puerto Vallarta, N = 88,686; stratified random samples of n = 364 D.C.I. users and n = 100 hotel users), exposure (statutory water valuation, municipal connection-fee schedules, increasing-block tariff regimes, and domestic subsidy eligibility rules), outcomes (bill payment tiers, perceived affordability, and perceived supply continuity/security), and study design (cross-sectional socio-legal and stratified random user survey study) are clearly identified.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with an English title and abstract on PDF pages 1-2). Eligible under Criterion 10 because translation from the clean Spanish digital full text is directly feasible and the study contributes primary socio-legal empirical evidence on municipal tariff, connection-cost, and subsidy-eligibility rules; translation method and translator should be logged in extraction_note at data extraction.

study_design: Cross-sectional socio-legal regulatory analysis and stratified random user survey study
population_and_sample: Users of the municipal drinking water and sewerage utility SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico (finite population N = 88,686 user accounts; two stratified random survey samples comprising n = 364 domestic, residential-domestic, commercial, and industrial [D.C.I.] users and n = 100 hotel users)
exposure: Legal valuation of water and municipal utility tariff, connection-fee, contracting, and domestic subsidy-eligibility rules (Ley de Aguas Nacionales, Ley de Ingresos del Municipio de Puerto Vallarta 2025, and RPSPAPDATDARMPV)
outcome: Approximate water and sanitation tariff payments and tariff-block distribution, perceived tariff affordability, and perceived security/continuity of drinking water supply upon payment
rationale: This socio-legal empirical study satisfies all inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading of Criterion 2. It examines household/domestic (alongside commercial, industrial, and hotel) access to municipal drinking water and sanitation services in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico (c1), analyzes concrete rule-type legal and tariff mechanisms—connection fees, contracting requirements, increasing-block volumetric tariffs, and eligibility screening rules for domestic tariff subsidies under the municipal utility regulation RPSPAPDATDARMPV and the 2025 Municipal Revenue Law (c2)—and pairs this legal analysis with primary stratified random survey data from 364 D.C.I. users and 100 hotel users (c3, c5) reporting approximate bill tiers, perceived tariff affordability, and perceived supply continuity/security upon bill payment (c4). Although published in Spanish (with an English abstract), full-text translation is directly feasible and the study is eligible under Criterion 10 (c6).
